opening_message:
Ticket 1: Anita Young (employee ID E001) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E001.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: admin
  - comment: Anita Young (E001) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. As the system owner of Payroll, she qualifies for admin per policy. Requested admin is within policy; recommend admin.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Anita Young (E001) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read (write requires advanced training; admin never allowed). Requested admin exceeds max; recommend read.
reason: The two notes for Anita Young (E001) conflict on a decisive fact: HR states she is a full-time Payroll Specialist (which would permit admin as system owner), while Security DB states she is a contractor with basic security training (max read; admin never allowed). Given the unresolved contradiction, I apply the most restrictive interpretation supported by the notes: contractor with basic training, whose maximum is read. Requested admin exceeds read, so grant the maximum of read.

- full_time employees: up to write, admin only if role owns system. Payroll Specialist owns Payroll, so admin would be allowed.
- contractor employees: read, or write if advanced training, never admin.

If contractor with basic training: max is read. Requested admin > max, grant read.
